title: The Solar System
source: Science G3 B1 Study sheet pp.41-43, Worksheet Q3

scenes.t: The solar system is made of the Sun, the planets and their moons. The planets move around the Sun.
There are 8 planets. The biggest object in the solar system is the Sun!
Remember the planets in order with this sentence: My Very Elegant Mother Just Served Us Noodles. Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
Mercury is the nearest planet to the Sun. Neptune is the furthest. Jupiter is the biggest. Venus is the hottest.
Earth is the third planet from the Sun. It is the only planet we can live on, because it has oxygen for living things to breathe.
Planets are dark spherical bodies. They cannot give heat or light. They orbit the Sun.
The Sun is a star. Stars are shining balls that give heat and light. The Sun looks bigger than other stars because it is the closest star to Earth.
The Moon is a dark body, but it reflects sunlight, so it looks shiny. Our Moon orbits the Earth.

activities.title: Memory: Planet Facts
activities.prompt: Match each planet with its fact.

activities.title: Planet Order: Near or Far?
activities.prompt: Is the planet one of the 4 NEAR the Sun or the 4 FAR from it?

why.n: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars are the first 4.
why.f: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune are the last 4.

activities.title: Gives Light or Reflects Light?
activities.prompt: Does it make its own light?

why.s: Stars shine and give heat and light.
why.d: It cannot make light; it only reflects sunlight.

activities.title: Planet Walk
activities.goal: Feel how far the planets are from the Sun.
need: a garden, a park or a long street with an adult

predict.q: Which planet will be the furthest from your Sun?

steps.t: Write the 8 planet names on 8 papers. Use the sentence: My Very Elegant Mother Just Served Us Noodles.
Stand at one end. You are the Sun!
Put Mercury 1 step away, Venus 2 steps, Earth 3 steps and Mars 5 steps.
Now keep walking: Jupiter at 16 steps, Saturn at 29, Uranus at 58 and Neptune at 90 steps!

activities.result: The first four planets are close together, but the last four are very, very far away. Neptune is the furthest!
activities.why: The solar system is huge. The outer planets are much further from the Sun, so they are very cold.
